answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the pulse identifier and voids the later submissions, which means the operator pays for 213 runs and collects one. Because the harbor index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the wander audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 213 answers need 213 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
